title: VToT: Automatic Verilog Generation via LLMs with Tree of Thoughts Prompting
problem: LLMs struggle with Verilog code generation due to poor performance on hardware description languages; standard Chain of Thought prompting fails to capture hierarchical hardware design constraints and the abstraction gap between natural language and HDL.
motivation: Automatic hardware design would accelerate chip development; LLM performance on HDLs lags programming languages and existing prompting techniques don't capture hardware-specific constraints.
method: Verilog Tree of Thoughts (VToT) structured prompting technique embeds hierarchical design constraints directly into prompts. Addresses CoT limitations by explicitly modeling hardware design structure and dependencies.
key_novelty: Hierarchical constraint-aware prompting (Tree of Thoughts) tailored for hardware description language code generation.
contributions: VToT prompting method embedding hierarchical hardware design constraints
75.9% correctness at pass@5 on RTLLM benchmark (+10.4% improvement)
52.4% correctness at pass@1 on VerilogEval (+8.9%), 65.4% at pass@5 (+9.6%)
State-of-the-art Verilog generation performance from LLMs

metrics.accuracy: 75.9% pass@5 RTLLM, 52.4% pass@1 VerilogEval, 65.4% pass@5 VerilogEval

limitations: Evaluation limited to two fixed benchmarks; scalability to industrial designs and real-world circuit complexity unclear.
primary_theme: LLM-based Verilog generation via constraint-aware hierarchical prompting
